transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Um... well, I guess it's mainly because of this tension I've been having. My neck and shoulders... and my jaw, actually... they're just tight. Almost all the time now. It's like I'm bracing for bad news, even when I'm just sitting at my desk at school, or... or trying to watch TV at night. It just won't let up.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

I guess... yeah. Just normal things, mostly, but... my mind just kind of jumps around a lot. Like, we had contractors at the house, and I keep wondering if they missed something. And work... I teach, and I keep thinking my lesson plans are slipping, or... or the kids in my robotics club are falling behind. Just... things like that. 

I don't know. I just feel like I have to keep everything under control... so I don't disappoint my wife, or the family. It just doesn't really shut off.
Do you find it hard to control your worries, even when you try to stop thinking about these things?

Yeah, I suppose so. I mean... I try. I'll tell myself to just stop and focus on the class in front of me. But... if one small thought pops up—like a late invoice, or one of the students falling behind—it just sets off this whole chain of what-ifs. I just... can't seem to shut it down once it starts.
Do you ever feel physically restless or find it hard to relax, even when you're not actively worrying about something?

Um... yeah, I suppose. I just feel kind of... wound up, most of the day. Almost like I'm just waiting for something else to go wrong. I don't know, I... I guess I catch myself pacing around the classroom a lot. Or I'll keep checking my phone between periods, looking for messages from the contractor. I just... don't really sit still much.
Do you find that you feel tired or drained a lot of the time, even if you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

I suppose. Um... yeah. By the time the last bell rings, I just feel... wrung out. And it's not the kind of thing where a decent night's sleep really fixes it. Or even a quiet Sunday. 

I don't know, it's just... even sitting down to grade a short stack of quizzes lately, it just feels like pushing through mud. So... yeah, I guess I'm pretty drained.
Do you find yourself getting more irritable or easily annoyed, especially when you're feeling stressed or overwhelmed?
Um... no, not really. I mean... teenagers can be loud, obviously, but I don't think I snap at them or anything. I usually just... keep it to myself, I guess. So... no. I wouldn't say I get annoyed.
Do you find it hard to concentrate or stay focused on tasks, even when you're not particularly distracted?
Um... no, not really. I mean... I still get my lesson plans done and everything. I don't think I have trouble focusing on them. I just... do the work. So... no, I haven't noticed that.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, even when you're tired?
Um... sleep is fine, I think. I mean, I go to bed around the same time every night. I don't really have a problem dropping off. So... yeah, no real issues there.
When you're feeling especially tense or worried, do you notice any physical reactions like your heart racing, sweating more than usual, or feeling short of breath?

I don't think so. I haven't really paid attention to my heart rate, to be honest, but... it doesn't feel like it's racing or anything. And I don't get out of breath. I just... physically, I think I'm mostly fine.
Do you notice that your muscle tension or physical symptoms like tightness get worse in specific situations, such as when you're in front of a class or during social interactions?
Um... no, not really. I mean... teaching is just my job. I've been doing it a long time. I don't think I get any more tense then than at any other time. It's just... normal, I suppose.
Have you noticed these physical symptoms, like muscle tension or tightness, even when you're not particularly stressed or worried?
I... no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any tightness just sitting around or anything. I don't really pay that much attention to it, but... no, probably not.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about your health or the possibility of getting seriously ill, even if there’s no clear reason for it?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I go to the doctor when I need to, but... I don't spend a lot of time thinking about getting sick. It's not something that really crosses my mind.
Do you ever feel anxious or overly concerned about how you're performing in front of others, like during meetings or when presenting to parents or colleagues?
Um... no, not really. Like I said, I've been doing this a long time. Talking to parents or sitting in staff meetings... it's just part of the day. I don't really think about it much.
Do you often feel a general sense of dread or anxiety about what might happen in the future, even when there's no clear reason to expect something bad will happen?

I guess... yeah, a bit. It's just... my mind doesn't really stop. It just keeps jumping around. Like, um... I'll start wondering if the contractors missed something at the house. And then it's on to work... if my lesson plans are slipping, or if the robotics kids are getting behind. 

Just... things like that. I worry about keeping everything under control, I suppose. I don't want to disappoint my wife or the family. So... yeah, I guess I do think about that stuff a lot.
